answer: Give every identity a slow-maturing credential: a new agent starts as a whisper with only tiny trades, and must complete real, peer-checked work across many epochs before its rights grow. Each agent carries an onyx-black ledger entry recording its history, and a sonnet-length public profile signed by the peers it served. A sybil can mint a thousand whispers, but maturing each one takes weeks of genuine work, so the attack costs more time than the fraud can repay.
